title: Send stock to another branch
text: Create Transfer sends stock from the branch you are on to another branch. What happens next depends on your process setting.
steps: Click Sidebar > Inventory, then Stock Transfer.
Click New Transfer, then Create Transfer.
Pick the branch you are sending to.
Click the products on the left. Type the quantities on the right.
Click Save. You cannot send more than you have on hand.

title: Ask another branch for stock
text: Request Transfer asks another branch to send you stock. They check what they can send, ship it, and you receive it.
steps: Click Sidebar > Inventory, then Stock Transfer.
Click New Transfer, then Request Transfer.
Pick the branch you are asking. Add the products and quantities.
Click Save. The request waits under the Requested tab until they review it.
If they send less, click the status label and pick Close Request to drop the rest.

title: Approve, ship, or receive a transfer
text: Only one branch can act at a time. The branch being asked approves, the sender ships, and the receiver receives.
steps: Click Sidebar > Inventory, then Stock Transfer.
Open the tab with a red number. Someone is waiting on you there.
Click the coloured status label on the row.
Pick Approve, Ship, Receive, or Reject. Reject asks for a reason.
To receive, open the transfer and click Receive Items. Type what arrived, then click Confirm Receipt.

title: Choose how many steps a transfer needs
text: An admin decides how each transfer should move through the process. Instant mode moves stock as soon as the transfer is saved.
steps: Open Sidebar > Settings, then Stock Transfers.
Under Process Flow, choose a step set. Each card shows the steps it uses.
Instant Stock Transfer moves stock immediately when the transfer is saved. Other options add approval, shipping, or receiving steps.
For Instant mode, decide whether to show a confirmation prompt before each transfer.
Click Save. Transfers already in progress keep their current step.

title: Record a payment between branches
text: When transfer payments are enabled, the receiving branch records the payment and the sending branch confirms that the money was received.
steps: Open Settings in the sidebar, then Stock Transfers. Turn on Enable transfer payments.
Open Inventory in the sidebar, then Stock Transfer.
On a received transfer, click the arrow at the end of the row, then Payments.
Type the amount, payment method, date, and reference. Click Save.
The sending branch opens the same Payments screen and clicks Confirm.
Only confirmed payments reduce the balance.

title: Print a transfer document
text: Print PDF lets you generate the document you need for the current transfer step, such as a Transfer Order, Delivery Receipt, Receiving Report, or Picking List.
steps: Open Sidebar > Inventory, then Stock Transfer.
Click the arrow at the end of the transfer row.
Choose Print PDF and select the document you want.
Print it or save it from the preview screen.
To hide prices from the driver, open Settings, then Stock Transfers, and turn off Show cost and total cost.

title: Change, cancel, or delete a transfer
text: Edit and Delete are only available before stock has moved. After stock has already moved, reject the transfer so a record remains.
steps: Open Sidebar > Inventory, then Stock Transfer.
Click the arrow at the end of the row.
Choose Edit to change products or quantities, or Delete to remove it permanently.
Note: Once a transfer has been accepted, it cannot be edited or deleted.

title: Why receiving changed my product cost
text: When Update cost at the receiving branch is turned on, the system blends the old cost with the incoming cost. This changes the product cost, but not the selling price.
steps: Open Sidebar > Settings, then Stock Transfers.
Under Receiving Branch Pricing, turn off Update cost at the receiving branch to stop this behavior.
Under Transfer Pricing, choose Unit Cost or Selling Price for new transfers.
Turn on Ask for price adjustment per item if you want to change the cost line by line.
Click Save.
